title: Nicolas Rinaudo - Programming a language
excerpt: In the past couple of years, I’ve had to implement two (very simple) programming languages for two different companies. I found the experience to be extremely fun, and have thus decided to study the subject a little more in depth - because yes, that is how a reasonable person does it: only after I’m done solving a problem (twice, no less!) will I study how one should actually go about it.
content_html:
• This is the companion article for this talk.
  • The full code for this series can be viewed here.

In the past couple of years, I’ve had to implement two (very simple) programming languages for two different companies. I found the experience to be extremely fun, and have thus decided to study the subject a little more in depth - because yes, that is how a reasonable person does it: only after I’m done solving a problem (twice, no less!) will I study how one should actually go about it.

And since it’s a fun thing to study, I’ve started giving informal live coding sessions on the subject at work. This series will follow these sessions, as I find it a good and motivating way to prepare them.

  • Introduction
  • Representing source code
  • Taking decisions
  • Naming things
  • Reusing code
  • Repeating actions
  • Identifying invalid programs
  • Inferring types
  • Enforcing typing rules in the AST
  • Producing a typed AST
  • Interpreting a typed AST
